Maintenance Report — MNT-0012-001

Asset: WELL-0012 (SW-23 Well 012, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 06 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 07 Jan 2023 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 20 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0012-0012 on 2023-01-05 Report written: 08 Jan 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0012-0012 at 11:15 on 2023-01-05 found crude oil on the pad: about 12.0% of the pad area, estimated 6.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 346 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 277 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 4.2 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0012-001 (WS-06).
  • 4 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.26% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0012-010

Asset: WELL-0012 (SW-23 Well 012, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 09 Feb 2024 08:00 · Finished: 20 Mar 2024 00:00 · Well stopped for this job: 952 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0012-0068 on 2024-02-08 Report written: 20 Mar 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0012-0068 showed the wellhead at 22.0 °C with the air at 12.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 38 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Review sand control on this well.
  • Send the old pump for teardown.
